breaking: ENERGY MARKETS: Brent crude rose to around $106.60 a barrel in early Wednesday trading amid renewed concern about Middle East energy supplies.
MIDDLE EAST: Recent Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia have increased concerns about regional security and oil-export routes.

DANGOTE IPO: The planned $1.6 billion share offering continues to attract retail investor interest, with the application deadline extended to 27 October.
ASIAN MARKETS: Shares edged higher as some technology and artificial-intelligence chipmakers recovered following a recent sell-off.
US ECONOMY: Investors are watching US inflation figures for further clues about the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions.

featured.title: Dangote Refinery Reports Major Profit Turnaround as Global Fuel Demand Rises
featured.content: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery reported a net profit of $4.73 billion for January to September 2026, compared with a $117.2 million loss in the same period last year. Revenue more than doubled to $22.48 billion, according to unaudited results reported by Reuters. The company has benefited from strong demand and international fuel-supply disruptions, including exports of jet fuel to Western Europe. Its planned public offering is expected to raise approximately $1.6 billion. The figures are unaudited, and the proposed share offering carries investment risk.

articles.title: Houthi Attacks Raise Fresh Concerns Over Saudi Security and Energy Supplies
articles.content: Renewed missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement have placed Saudi Arabia's air defences and critical infrastructure under pressure. The Associated Press reports that the attacks have caused deaths and disrupted daily life. The security situation is also attracting attention because Saudi Arabia is a major oil producer and an important participant in international energy markets. The precise consequences for exports and shipping will depend on how the situation develops.

articles.title: Middle East Tensions Keep Global Energy Markets on Alert
articles.content: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as investors assessed the risk of further disruption to energy supplies following renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Reuters reported Brent crude at around $106.60 a barrel and US crude near $94.96 in early trading. Prices can change throughout the day, and these figures represent a reported market snapshot rather than a closing price. Any prolonged disruption to oil production, export routes or shipping could affect transport, manufacturing, electricity and household costs.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Posts $4.73 Billion Nine-Month Net Profit
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery reported a net profit of $4.73 billion for the first nine months of 2026, compared with a $117.2 million loss in the same period of 2025. Revenue rose to $22.48 billion, while operating cash flow also increased significantly, according to unaudited results reported by Reuters. The refinery has benefited from strong demand for refined products and supply disruptions associated with the Iran war. The company says it plans to double capacity by 2029. The results are unaudited and should be read in that context.

articles.title: Dangote IPO Draws Retail Interest as Investors Weigh Risks
articles.content: The planned Dangote Petroleum Refinery initial public offering is expected to raise around $1.6 billion and could become one of Africa's largest share offerings. Reuters reported that intense public interest has previously contributed to outages on some digital investment platforms. Financial-sector observers say broader retail participation could help deepen African capital markets, but investors should consider valuation, business performance, market conditions and the possibility of losses. Strong demand for shares does not guarantee future returns, and investors should review the official offer documents before making decisions.

articles.title: Global Markets Await US Inflation Data
articles.content: Investors are watching US consumer-price data for clues about the direction of interest rates. Reuters reported that Asian shares rose modestly on Wednesday as several technology and AI-related chipmakers recovered from recent losses. However, elevated oil prices and uncertainty about inflation limited gains. Higher inflation could complicate decisions for the Federal Reserve and affect borrowing costs, currencies, government bonds and stock markets. Market conditions remain fluid, and the inflation figures may change expectations once released.

articles.title: Asian Shares Recover as Technology Stocks Rebound
articles.content: Asian equity markets edged higher on Wednesday, supported by a recovery among some semiconductor companies linked to artificial intelligence. Reuters reported gains in South Korea's Kospi and a modest rise in Japan's Nikkei. The improvement followed a recent technology-led sell-off, although investors remained cautious because of high oil prices and upcoming US inflation data. Market movements reflect changing expectations and do not establish a sustained recovery.

articles.title: AI Chipmakers Recover After Recent Market Sell-Off
articles.content: Several companies in the artificial-intelligence semiconductor supply chain recovered in Asian trading on Wednesday. Reuters reported gains among South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, while Japan's Kioxia was broadly steady. The sector remains sensitive to demand expectations, investment spending, technology competition and wider financial-market conditions. Investors are also assessing how interest rates and energy costs could affect the outlook for technology businesses.

articles.title: US Inflation Figures Could Shape Interest-Rate Expectations
articles.content: US inflation data due on Wednesday is being closely watched by investors seeking clues about the Federal Reserve's next policy decisions. Reuters reported that markets were considering the possibility of another rate increase later in the year, while Treasury yields and the dollar reflected shifting expectations. The actual effect will depend on the published figures and subsequent comments from policymakers. Interest-rate decisions can influence mortgages, business loans, government borrowing and international investment.

articles.title: Europe Watches Oil Prices and Refined-Fuel Supply Risks
articles.content: European households and businesses remain exposed to changes in global energy prices. Oil-market uncertainty can affect the cost of transport, logistics, aviation and industrial production, while disruptions to refined-fuel supplies can create additional pressure in individual markets. Nigeria's Dangote refinery has recently supplied jet fuel to Western Europe amid international supply disruptions, according to Reuters. Its growing export role highlights the connections between African refining capacity and European energy security.

articles.title: Nigeria's Refining Industry Takes on a Larger International Role
articles.content: Nigeria's refining sector is attracting international attention as Dangote Petroleum Refinery supplies domestic customers and exports refined products to overseas markets. The refinery's reported nine-month results show how international demand and supply disruptions can influence its performance. For Nigeria, the wider questions include reliable crude supply, domestic fuel prices, foreign-exchange exposure, export earnings and the extent to which industrial growth benefits households. A stronger refining industry can improve supply options, but it does not insulate the country completely from global oil-price movements.
